requirement: The Habeas crate MUST use the same `habeas::validate()` Cargo integration test as downstream projects to check its own requirements and evidence.
rationale: The requirement has one obligation. The Habeas crate MUST check its own requirements and evidence through the same `habeas::validate()` Cargo integration test that downstream projects use. The reviewed test is `tests/habeas.rs#fn[habeas]`. It is marked `{test}` for `requirements.integration.self_test`. It is a `#[test]` in the crate's `tests/` directory, so Cargo runs it as an integration test. Its whole body is `habeas::validate();`, which is the same entry point downstream projects call. The test passes only if `validate()` succeeds, so it exercises the self-check and enforces its outcome. The test is the required usage, so there is no further behavior to assert. The obligation has no other conditions, modes, or failure cases. How `validate()` behaves is covered by `requirements.integration.validate` and its own tests, so I did not reassess it here.
